newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends session where it began.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends session where it began.

text.p: A listless New Zealand dollar ended on Friday almost precisely where it started.
At 5.00 p.m. (0400 GMT) it was at US$0.7090/97 against a 0.7090/95 opening while the Trade-Weighted Index was two basis points stronger at 66.94.
Trade was light and in a narrow band.
Dealers said the Kiwi would be driven next week by a likely breaking of the political impasse which has existed since the October 12 election.

New Zealand First, with the balance of power, is expected to select its coalition preference from the ruling conservative National Party or the centre-left Labour Party by around the middle of the week.
A choice for Labour would see the Kiwi sold sharply and a National Party selection would result in a rally, dealers said.
But one said that any rally on a National option was likely to be short-lived as the fiscal position is almost certain to deteriorate following concessions to NZ First.
Treasury's December Economic and Fiscal Update on Monday is unlikely to add much more information than the pre-election update and could be out of date very quickly, economists said.
